\abstract{\textbf{Motivation:} As sequencing data and reference collections grow, from complete genomes to pangenomes, finding seeds, the exact matches between a query and a reference from which reads are mapped and genomes are aligned, has become a central step of sequence analysis. Many kinds of seeds are in use, from sampled k-mers such as minimizers to maximal exact matches, and each is computed by its own specialized tool, with its own index and output format. And as processors gain wider vector units and deeper memory hierarchies, the speed of seeding depends increasingly on how well an implementation uses each core.\\
\textbf{Results:} We present sporos, one library that computes all of these seeds exactly, built around each core's vector units and memory parallelism. Its key contribution counts the copies of a MEM's string from the MEMs themselves: a string occurs in the reference once for every MEM whose query interval contains its own, so frequency-capped MEMs need no additional index. On a single core of an Intel Skylake-X processor, sporos computed minimizers and syncmers 1.8--2.3 times faster than simd-minimizers, looked up seeds 3.9 times faster than minimap2, found MEMs between two human chromosomes 1 2.0--2.4 times faster than copMEM2, MEMs and MUMs 4.2--43 times faster than MUMmer4 with identical output, frequency-capped MEMs 121--176 times faster than Mumemto, and SMEMs of short reads 4.8 times faster than minibwa.\\
\textbf{Availability and implementation:} sporos is free software under the MIT license, written in Mojo with C, Python and command-line interfaces, at \url{https://github.com/kokyriakidis/sporos}.}
